metaData.title: Ozark Valley Arts Council membership check in

sentences.text: Good afternoon, thanks for finding the slot at short notice.
I have half an hour down and I would like to spend most of it on how the autumn intake is going.
Afternoon. Half an hour is fine, I have a studio visit at two but not before.
I made a short list this morning so I do not forget the things that only come to mind when somebody asks.
Start me off with the intake then. Where did you land against the target the board set you?
We are at two thousand nine hundred paid members, which is about sixty ahead of where we planned to be.
The growth is nearly all in the working artist category rather than the patron category, which is not what anyone predicted.
Patrons are flat and have been flat for two years, and the board has stopped pretending that is a surprise.
Sixty ahead is a decent place to be in September.
Is the working artist category behaving differently once people are in, or does it look like the rest of the base?
It behaves quite differently. They join for the exhibition calls and the studio insurance, and they renew if they got something out of both.
Patrons join because somebody they know asked them to, and they renew for the same reason, which makes them steady but hard to grow.
That matches what I see at councils of your size. Has the insurance benefit been used much?
Two hundred and forty claims of one kind or another since January, mostly small.
One member had a kiln fire and that single claim justified the whole scheme in the eyes of the finance committee.
Good. Now, you said you had a list. What is on it?
The first thing is the member directory, and it is the one that comes up at every regional meeting.
Our members cannot look one another up by county or by the craft they work in, so the directory is only useful if you already know the person's name.
A weaver in the south of the state wants to find the other weavers within an hour's drive, and there is no way for her to do that on her own.
Our office answers about fifteen of those requests a month by hand, and the answer we give is a guess based on who we happen to remember.
Let me make sure I have that right, because I will be passing it on to people who were not here.
You want a member to be able to search other members by where they are and by what they make, without going through your office.
That is exactly it.
The information is already sitting on the member record, because we ask for the county and the discipline when somebody joins.
It simply is not something anybody can search on, so it only ever comes back out when a person on staff goes looking for it.
Understood. I will write it up today and put your words on it rather than my summary of them.
If you have two or three of those requests in writing, send them to priya.natarajan@momentivesoftware.example.org and I will attach them.
I will pull three from the last fortnight. They read almost identically, which I think makes the point better than anything I could write.
Helpful. What else was on the list?
The autumn festival, which is in five weeks and is the largest thing we run.
Eleven hundred people over two days across six venues in the town, and every one of them needs a badge on the way in.
That is already a support case so I will not use your time on it here, but it is the thing keeping me awake.
I saw the case come through this morning and it is with the right group.
I will keep an eye on it from my side and chase it if it goes quiet for more than a couple of days.
That is all I need on it. It is a known quantity, just an unpleasant one.
So my actions are the directory write up and keeping the festival case moving.
Anything else before you go and look at a studio?
Nothing else. Thank you for making the time on a Thursday.
